# Reproducibility {#sec-reproducibility}



Anyone who runs the survey chapters should get the same numbers. Four things make that
possible.

## The same packages

R packages change between versions, and a new version can change a result. Install the
packages once, from the R console:

```{.r}
install.packages(c(
  "broom", "dplyr", "furrr", "future", "gtsummary", "haven", "knitr", "mice",
  "mitml", "parallelly", "purrr", "rmarkdown", "sqldf", "srvyr", "survey", "tibble",
  "tidylog", "tidyr"
))
```

The survey chapters need dplyr 1.2.0 or later, for `dplyr::recode_values()`. The
session information at the end of this appendix lists the exact versions used to build
the book. When you report results, report the versions you used.

## The same random numbers: seeds

Multiple imputation draws random values. `chapters/survey/_common.R` sets the same seed
(2024) at the start of every chapter. The imputation runs one task per imputation in
parallel, and `furrr::furrr_options(seed = seed)` gives each task its own reproducible
random-number stream, so the imputed values are the same whether your computer has 2
cores or 16.

## Smoke tests

A full render takes time because of the imputation. Before a full run, a smoke test
checks that every survey chapter works:

```sh
quarto render chapters/survey --profile smoke
```

The `smoke` profile (`_quarto-smoke.yml` and `_environment-smoke` in the book's root
folder) sets the number of imputations to 2 and writes the book to `_book-smoke/` and the
data to `data/brfss/processed-smoke/`. Every page of a smoke book says "SMOKE TEST" in
its title. The number of imputations is set in one place (`N_IMPUTATIONS`, read in
`_common.R`), and every count in the code and text follows it.

## Reusing expensive calculations

Expensive R chunks use `#| cache: true`, Quarto's standard knitr cache. The setup
records the chapter's R code, contents of its input files, shared settings, R and package
versions, and survey options in `cache.extra`. These inputs invalidate cached results
when the analysis changes. Editing prose does not.

Full runs store their caches in `data/brfss/processed/cache/`; smoke runs use
`data/brfss/processed-smoke/cache/`. Setup and file-saving chunks always run, so later
chapters still receive their inputs on a cached render. Only rendering uses the cache;
running individual lines in the R console executes them normally.

To recalculate all cached chunks in the survey chapters:

```sh
quarto render chapters/survey --cache-refresh
```

See the [Quarto caching documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/caching.html)
for details. Validate the initial calculation before relying on cached results.

## Rendering the book without the data

The survey chapters set `freeze: auto` (in `chapters/survey/_metadata.yml`). After
someone renders them with the data, Quarto stores their results in `_freeze/`. When that
folder is shared with the book, `quarto render` reuses the stored results, so the whole
book renders on a computer without the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)
files. Rendering the folder directly (`quarto render chapters/survey`) always re-runs the
chapters.
